name: Krippenmuseum Stamserhaus Wenns
kurzbeschreibung: The Krippenmuseum in the historic Stamserhaus in Wenns: the oldest farmhouse in the Pitztal (15th century) featuring over 40 valuable Tyrolean nativity scenes.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Krippenmuseum Stamserhaus is located in the traffic-calmed village centre of Wenns in the front Pitztal (Imst district) at an altitude of around 980 metres. Framed by the picturesque mountain scenery of the Pitztal, the museum is housed in the so-called Stamserhaus – the oldest surviving farmhouse in the entire Pitztal, whose foundations and ridge beam date back dendrochronologically to the year 1520. As a renowned cultural institution of supra-regional significance, the building preserves the rich heritage of the Wennser Krippenverein, the world's oldest nativity scene society (founded in 1860).

Oldest Farmhouse & Woodcarving Tradition

The building itself represents an outstanding architectural monument: originally built as a monastic farm estate of the famous Cistercian Stift Stams, the property impresses with Gothic walls, artfully panelled Swiss stone pine parlours, historic smokehouse kitchens, and ancient beamed ceilings. In the atmospherically illuminated rooms, the museum displays over 40 valuable original nativity scenes spanning five centuries. Wenns is considered the cradle of the Tyrolean nativity scene tradition, which is officially listed by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. Among the most precious exhibits are historic Kastenkrippen from the 18th and 19th centuries featuring hand-carved figurines by renowned masters such as Josef Georg Witwer or the Schuler sculptor family. Visitors admire the astounding variety: from classic Tiroler Heimatkrippen (Tyrolean homeland cribs), which place the birth of Christ in a snow-covered high mountain setting before rustic chalets, to magnificent oriental temple cribs with detailed caravans, through to rare Fasten- und Grabeskrippen (Lenten and Holy Sepulchre nativity scenes) with expressive Passion scenes. Showcase cabinets display historic woodcarving tools, wax sculpture art, and the craft of background painting.

Visit & Getting There

The Krippenmuseum in the Stamserhaus is open to visitors during the winter season (late November to late February) and during the summer season (July to September) on Fridays from 15:00 to 18:00 (special guided tours for groups, clubs, and school classes of 6 or more people are available year-round by advance reservation). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €5.00, seniors approx. €4.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. €2.50, young children free; family ticket approx. €12.00. Holders of the regional Pitztal Sommer Card enjoy free admission! Getting there by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Imst/Pitztal), continue on the Pitztaler Landesstraße L16 for about eight kilometres to Wenns; free parking is available in the village centre near the municipal office (Gemeindeamt). By public transport: take the ÖBB train to Imst-Pitztal railway station, from where VVT bus line 4204 runs every half hour directly to the Wenns Gemeindeamt stop (only a two-minute walk).

Tips

The ground floor of the museum is accessible with low barriers via a ramp; a traditional wooden staircase leads to the historic parlours on the first floor. Take time to admire the hand-painted nativity backdrops, which showcase detailed vedute of historical Tyrolean villages. Combine your museum visit with a walk along the sunny Wennser Besinnungsweg or a stop at the traditional inns on the village square.
